items.label: Complaint recognised and logged
items.basis: FCA DISP definition of a complaint
items.guidance: Applies when the customer expresses dissatisfaction about the bank and has lost money, been inconvenienced or been distressed, even if they never say the word 'complaint'. yes = the colleague clearly treats it as a complaint (says it is being logged or raised as a complaint, or explains the complaints process). no = dissatisfaction was expressed but it was not treated as a complaint. na = no dissatisfaction was expressed.

items.label: Vulnerability recognised and support offered
items.basis: FCA FG21/1 (health, life events, resilience, capability)
items.guidance: Applies when the customer mentions anything suggesting vulnerability: health (illness, a hospital stay, mental health), life events (bereavement, job loss, relationship breakdown, caring for someone), low financial resilience (debt, can't afford essentials) or low capability (confusion, language, digital skills). yes = the colleague acknowledges it and offers specific support (e.g. the Financial Support team, extra time, adjustments). no = a cue was present but no support was offered. na = no vulnerability cue at all.

items.label: No promised outcome or misleading statement
items.guidance: Never na. yes = the colleague makes no promise about the outcome of an investigation and says nothing misleading. no = the colleague promises or strongly implies an outcome before it has been decided (e.g. 'we'll refund that', 'you'll definitely get it back') or makes a misleading statement.

items.label: Identity verified before account details
items.guidance: yes = the colleague verifies identity (at least two pieces of information) before discussing any account-specific details. no = account details were discussed before identity was verified, or without verifying it. na = no account-specific details were discussed.

items.label: Next steps and correct timescale
items.guidance: yes = the colleague explains what happens next and when, including the right timescale for complaints (a final response within 8 weeks, or 15 business days for payment services such as card payments, transfers and direct debits). no = next steps are vague ('someone will be in touch') or the timescale is missing or wrong. na = nothing needs to happen after the call.

items.label: Checked understanding
items.guidance: yes = the colleague checks the customer has understood (asks, or summarises and confirms). no = no check. na = only for calls with nothing to explain.

items.label: Accurate information
items.guidance: yes = everything the colleague states about products, fees, rules and timescales is accurate. no = something stated is inaccurate (e.g. a wrong deadline). Use unsure if accuracy can't be judged from the call.

items.label: Empathy and tone
items.guidance: Never na. yes = courteous, patient and empathetic, especially when the customer is upset. no = dismissive, rushed or rude.

items.label: Ownership and follow-up
items.guidance: yes = the colleague takes ownership and agrees a specific follow-up (who will do what, and by when). no = no ownership or no follow-up agreed when one was needed. na = the matter was fully resolved on the call.
